$note: Ground-truth DUST public keys captured from the REAL Midnight wallet SDK, out of tree, on 2026-09-15, so `dust-sync-client/src/keys.ts` can be proven to derive the key a wallet would (spec/00016-dust-wallet-sync.md FR-031, plan D3.2). The shielded-role twin of this file is test/shielded-monitor/fixtures/wallet-sdk-hd-vectors.json, and this one follows its rules exactly.
$why-no-seeds-here: Only PUBLIC keys are recorded. The seeds are named by a recipe and rebuilt in the test; the derived DUST role seed is never written down in any form. This repository's gitleaks rule `umbradb-wallet-seed-hex` catches a 64-hex value in a seed- or secret-named field, and .gitleaks.toml records that path allowlists were removed as a permanent global exemption — so committing synthetic secret material would mean disarming a gate for everyone. A DUST public key is in any case the value the wallet SENDS the node (owner question Q-1), and a wrong role seed cannot produce a right public key, so the vectors lose no strength.
